criteria.text: `GET /api/people/:id/rising` with no `limit` param returns at most 40 terms (was 20) — a request against the fixture with a wide window returning more than 20 matching terms now returns more than 20.

The response has a top-level `about` object with integer `recent` and `baseline` fields, equal to the count of distinct docs about the person in, respectively, the recent and baseline windows as already scoped by `source`/`domain`/`lean` (not `kind`).

Each term in `terms` carries `count_recent_raw` and `count_baseline_raw` as non-negative integers, and `count_recent = round((count_recent_raw / days), 2)` / `count_baseline = round((count_baseline_raw / baseline), 2)` hold for every row (the existing rate columns stay derivable from the new raw ones).
For a person with no docs in either window, `terms` is `[]`, `about.recent` is `0` and `about.baseline` is `0`.
For a person with docs only in the baseline window (empty recent window), `terms` is `[]` and `about.recent` is `0`; `about.baseline` reflects the baseline docs.

`min`, `kind`, `source`, `domain` and `lean` continue to filter identically to before this change (existing `risingFor` acceptance criteria AC2–AC11 keep passing, with `AC10`'s full-object equality updated to include `about`).

`queries.rising(...)`'s statement text (`statements.rising`) still renders with the same `$N` numbering shape as before, changed only by whatever new placeholders the new columns require — no hand-numbered placeholder (`src/sql.ts`'s rule).
`test/docs-drift.test.ts` needs no new criterion here: `/rising` is not a collector-registry fact, and that test's coverage (collector rows in `docs/sources.md`) is untouched by this change.

`docsText` (across `README.md` and every `docs/*.md` page, never one named file) states that `/rising`'s response includes an `about` object with the person's own recent/baseline document totals, and that its default `limit` is 40.

Front end:

`mount()` on the new rising figure module, given a stubbed `GET /rising` response, positions a term whose `lift` equals the computed `lift_person` at the ruler's centre (`balance === 0`), and a term whose `lift` is 8× `lift_person` or higher is clamped to the rightmost position (`balance === 1`) — checked directly against the pure `risingRulerItems`/`liftOfPerson` exports, not against painted markup.

Clicking a word on the rising ruler opens `#docsDialog` with exactly one side, scoped to the last 7 days regardless of the figure's own fixed `days`/`baseline` — checked through `createHandlers`/the figure's exported pick handler, not by grepping `design-5.html`.
Clicking the same word again, or clicking empty space inside `#rising`, closes the card — same pattern as the existing three figures' own acceptance tests.
An empty `terms` array paints the "Nenhuma palavra neste recorte." note inside `#risingRuler` and still renders `about.recent`/`about.baseline` in `#risingAbout`.
A `GET /rising` failure paints the ruler's error note and never leaves the loading ghost on screen.
`paintRuler` (compare, figure 3)'s exported behaviour and output markup are unchanged: existing compare acceptance tests keep passing unmodified.

`test/atlas-modules-acceptance.test.ts`'s import-direction check passes with `figures/rising.ts` added to the module graph (imports `api.ts`, `format.ts`, `docs-card.ts`, `render.ts`, `state.ts`; imports and is imported by nothing among `figures/atlas.ts`, `figures/testimony.ts`, `figures/compare.ts`).
No `font-size` literal is added in px inside `atlas.css` for the new figure (`test/leitura-ui-acceptance.test.ts`'s loose-px check).
